name.primary: Yoghurt, Berry and Granola Cups for Two

summary: Vanilla yoghurt layered in two glasses with fresh berries and crunchy granola. Nothing is cooked: the only skill is spooning in layers, and the only rule that matters is to assemble just before eating so the granola stays crisp. Active time about 10 minutes; cook time none; chill time none; total about 10 minutes. Serves 2.

ingredients.note: The source uses vanilla nonfat yoghurt. Our gram figure is an editorial adaptation of its halved cup amount, not an exact conversion. Milk allergen.
The source also allows defrosted frozen strawberries in juice; this record uses fresh fruit only, to keep the no-cook version simple.
Our adaptation of the source's half pint.
Check the label: many contain wheat or other gluten cereals, tree nuts, peanuts, sesame or soy.

method.instruction: Tools: two clear glasses or jars of about 300 ml each, a sieve or colander, a small knife and board, and a dessert spoon. Rinse the berries under cold running water, drain them well and pat dry with paper towel, then hull and slice the strawberries and mix them with the other berries.
Spoon roughly a third of the yoghurt (about 60 g per glass) into the bottom of each glass. The source starts each glass with a yoghurt layer in the same way.
Add a layer of berries, then a layer of granola, then more yoghurt, and repeat until the glasses are full and all the ingredients are used. Finish with a few berries and a sprinkle of granola on top.
Serve straight away. The source's point, kept here, is that the granola softens once it sits on wet yoghurt; the practical cue is that it should still crunch when you eat it.

yield_note: Serves 2 in this adaptation. Source facts: the source serves 4, rates it easy, and gives 5 minutes total with no cooking. Our adaptation: every source quantity was halved (1½ US cups yoghurt, ½ cup strawberries, ½ pint other berries, ½ cup granola), then rounded to amounts sold in Australian supermarkets — 350 g yoghurt, 80 g strawberries, a 125 g punnet of berries and 50 g granola. Those grams are an approximate editorial choice, not a conversion the source states. Times in this record: active about 10 minutes (our allowance for washing fruit); cook none; chill none; total about 10 minutes. Storage (our conservative advice, not the source's): eat once assembled. Keep unused yoghurt sealed in the fridge and use it by its date; keep spare washed berries covered in the fridge and eat them within a day or two; keep granola airtight in the pantry. If an assembled cup must wait, cover it and refrigerate, and eat it the same day, accepting soft granola.

caveats: Nothing in this dessert is cooked, so the berries are eaten raw. Rinse them under running water just before use and keep everything cold until you assemble it.
This record uses fresh berries only. It does not cover frozen berries, which some food-safety authorities advise heating before eating; follow your own authority's advice if you substitute them.

Allergens: milk in the yoghurt. Granola often contains gluten cereals and may contain tree nuts, peanuts, sesame or soy; read the label for anyone with an allergy. A lactose-free or plant-based yoghurt is a possible substitute but has not been tried here.
